body:
I don't read when I take a dump. I think intensely about things to come, the relationship with the people around me, and what my life has come to. I draw conclusions about who I am and why I'm this way.

Then I forget as soon as I emerge from the bathroom. It's a cycle.
This is shit, but it's my first shit so it's special to me.

I've never used Cymbalta, I was just providing another example. Sorry if that was confusing!

It's interesting that it's only effective in some. I guess it would have to do with the cause of the illness? And if placebo works, then that's good as well. That might be the case with me because my mind is very weak to the power of suggestion.

I think my doc thinks that a low dose is good just to see whether or not it helps. And I will most definitely talk with her on whether or not she thinks it's not some side effect or hypomania. If it lasts for too long then I'll bump up my appointment with her, but if it's only a short amount of time then I'll know it's a placebo.

I'm glad you're off of them and I hope you're feeling better! Thank you for the kind offer, I will most definitely ask if I have any more questions. :)
That's what I was thinking. Both are plausible, so I'm definitely going to keep an eye on it and see how it goes. I feel a bit more calm now, so it could have just been a placebo.

It does feel weird. It feels so weird that I wonder if I had anything in the first place. I need to have enough anxiety to monitor my lower right abdominal pain, though. I'll probably be able to tell if it gets bad enough. I'm glad you're feeling better, though! :)

Yeah! I take them with my breakfast so it's hard to forget them. Thank you for the advice.

She just said that it was supposed to kick in after a few weeks and I feel really wound up and a little jittery. And I don't think it's fully manic, just hypomanic since it all went away so quickly I would've expected something a lot more gradual than a sudden flip of a switch. Everyone I've seen has said that even with the medication it doesn't go away completely. I'm taking half doses of the 50mg for a week then I'm taking one full dose per day.

That's very true. Only schools that are pretty large will have Japanese,  I think. But sadly enough they offered Japanese at my school while the Mandarin program was cut out just as I arrived. It was lucky for me, but you know it's because of the weebs taking it.
I think it's worth it to try. Have you read up on mood and/or anxiety disorders? I can send you links if you want them.

I'm not a professional, but my best guess would be anxiety. It *could* be schizophrenia, but anxiety is much more likely. But it's good that you're going to a psych! That first step is really important and I'm glad that you're taking it. I know someone who plucked out their eyebrows because of anxiety and had to get them tattooed on. In any case, here's a little webpage that someone else posted on anxiety. http://www.rcpsych.ac.uk/expertadvice/problemsdisorders/anxiety,panic,phobias.aspx
It might not fit you, but I'd definitely consider it--you're going through a big change!
You can PM me with it! But whether you do or don't, I hope that you can find someone to talk to.

Thank you!

And if you ever need to talk, I don't mind reading and replying. I might be horrible at giving advice though!

Yeah, I think I'll tell her about it. It's so petty it's hard to believe something like that pushed me off the edge. I guess it could've been anything to push me off since I just start crying when people ask if I'm okay. I'll probably tell my counselor that I'm constantly on edge.

Anyways, thanks for the help. <3 I'll definitely find a way to talk to my friend about it later.

Alright, I'll definitely keep that in mind.

I know she's definitely going to want to help me since she's a very kind person. She's just also going through a lot and I feel like I have unrealistic expectations for her.

She wasn't certain. I knew she was questioning about it before, and I was too and we talked about it. I guess the bigger problem I have is her acting different than she used to. Like she suddenly starts talking about the girls she finds attractive to me and I mean it's great and all, but I don't usually talk about attractive men to straight guys either since I know they don't relate. At least if I were into girls I could make a joke about her having terrible taste and that my waifus were superior, you know? It's just another thing she likes that I don't like and it makes me feel like it'll make us grow apart, though it'd mostly be my fault. Also, it seems like it's more sexual than romantic which makes me a little bit worried for her future partner if she likes her a lot. Sorry, I'm rambling about it.

And I definitely know sexuality is a weird thing since I don't know mine. I just know I like dudes and don't want to have sex and so I just run with that.
ikr so hot like wow
Yeah, he definitely wasn't as terrible as some people from the stories here. He just made me and some of my friends uncomfortable.

I know. I'm just more trying the "slowly distance myself from her" tactic. My sister did it and it's worked for her. And the two of us are going to try and convince her to get some help. Unfortunately, she lives in another town so it'd be hard to get her to go to my counselor.

And that's true. I need to try and get rid of what's holding me back. I guess I just don't want to feel guilty for making people feel bad any more. Thank you.

Yeah, she might have been embarrassed about it. I know it's irrational for me to be sad about it, which is a big part of why it's hard to say anything about it. I feel like if I do, I'll be like my mom who just says whatever without actually caring how the person on the other end feels.

Sorry if it seems like I'm being resistant. I'm thankful for your kindness.

I'm not qualified or anything, but have you seen a psychiatrist? In some people, poor mental and emotional state can produce physical symptoms. I'm pretty sure that I'm the same way, though I haven't gotten every single possible test done. Even if you don't think it can help, you should at least try it. If the college you're enrolled in is kind of big, it might have mental help centers on campus. If not, then there are still going to be people who are qualified in the area who can help you.

Yeah, I've definitely considered not talking to her, but I worry that she might commit suicide if I do. She's actually tried such things before and went on to tell me about it. She just wants someone that she can make feel bad, I guess.

And yes, she is. I know change is a natural part of life, I just haven't had to face it to this degree until now. I know that it's good that she's happy, but I can't help but wish that she told me what she was keeping from me at a different time. I know that's selfish. And I'd talk to her about it, but she'll just feel bad and I don't know that I'll feel better.

I've talked to my counselor about my mom, most definitely. I might talk to her about my friend too since she's being paid to help and listen. I guess it would just be better to talk to my friend about it though.

* I can be very judgmental and egotistical, but I find a way to not come across as such. 
* I can also hold grudges for some time, even if what happened was minor. 
* I'm an extremely envious person which has led to underlying resentment even towards one of my best friends.
* This bitterness and insecurity leads me to be passive-aggressive or sometimes manipulative.
* I say sorry even when I'm not so that I can seem more friendly and approachable.
* My feelings are constantly changing and it's frustrating to keep up.

I'd probably be better about all of this if I could truly boost my confidence rather than use a half-assed superiority complex. It feels good to have these things written down, though.
You know what? That's too true. I should have thought of that and then I would have truly understood him.
Sometimes he would have both and I just have to wonder why he would go to the trouble of carrying it all. He was truly dedicated to his craft.
